current_data_sources: Public web and open-source intelligence (public profiles, company sites)
Proprietary contact database of 1B+ records, refreshed monthly
Profile and company page scraping (Profile Scraper, Person/Company Profile URL Finder)

api_or_integration_evidence.quote: 80% of our customers embed the Icypeas API in their own product or automated workflows.
The API allows you to make single and bulk searches as well as being notified during a search.

newsletter_capability_detail: Searched the homepage feature list (Email Finder, Email Verifier, Reverse Email Lookup, Domain Scan, People Scraper, Company Scraper, Find People, Find Companies), pricing/credit table and api-doc.icypeas.com getting-started page, plus site:icypeas.com newsletter search. No newsletter ingestion, publication index, article corpus, sponsor tracking or entity extraction from editorial content is described anywhere.
verified_gap: Icypeas' own scope is person/domain contact records (emails, phones, profile and company data). It holds no newsletter publication index, article corpus, guest/sponsor mentions or publication momentum signal, so it cannot answer 'which newsletters wrote about company X'.

contact_route.note: Publicly listed under 'Contact Support' on the contact page; phone +33 668 467 845 also listed.

caveats: They are a contact-data vendor selling into GTM teams, so newsletter-derived company intelligence is adjacent input for their company enrichment rather than core product; budget authority may sit with the founders. newsletter_capability_detail: Searched hunter.io/our-data (the page that documents sourcing), /api, /mcp, /b2b-database and site:hunter.io newsletter. Newsletter appears only as outreach templates (newsletter-swap, sponsor-slot templates) and blog content, never as an ingested source or a data product.
verified_gap: Hunter documents its ingestion as crawling public web pages to extract professional contact information, with source records attached. It has no newsletter publication index, no article-level topic/guest/sponsor extraction and no publication momentum tracking, so it cannot show which newsletters covered a company or who sponsors them.

likely_buyer_role: Head of Data or VP Product for the Data Platform/API (data sourcing and enrichment roadmap)

contact_route.note: Address publicly listed in Hunter's site footer (verified on the pricing page); hunter.io/contact is a form, no named data lead published.

caveats: Hunter already crawls the open web and sells 'signals', so they could build newsletter extraction in-house; the pitch must be corpus + entity resolution + momentum history rather than raw crawling. Their API is a real integration surface (MCP, Zapier, CRMs) but they are a much larger vendor with in-house data engineering.

evidence.quote: Point it at a URL. Zyte API picks the leanest access strategy that works and escalates only when the website demands it.
Automatic extraction supports AI-powered extraction of e-commerce, article and job posting data from any website

likely_buyer_role: Head of Data Acquisition / VP Product for Zyte Data (buys or builds vertical datasets)

contact_route.note: No named data lead or email published; form is the only public sales route found.

caveats: Weakest fit of the three: Zyte sells extraction capacity, not curated datasets, and already extracts article content on request, so the gap is unverified rather than confirmed. A newsletter corpus could be raw material for their managed Zyte Data service, but they more plausibly build it than buy it. No public pricing for Zyte Data and no named buyer.
